title: Environmental large language model Evaluation (ELLE) dataset: A Benchmark for Evaluating Generative AI applications in Eco-environment Domain
extended_summary:
This paper addresses the lack of a standardized and reliable evaluation framework for generative AI and large language models (LLMs) in the ecological and environmental domain. The authors argue that existing evaluations do not sufficiently measure domain professionalism, clarity, feasibility, or applicability for specialized eco-environment tasks, limiting trustworthy comparison of models and their derivatives such as fine-tuned models and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems.

To address this gap, the paper introduces the ELLE-QA Benchmark, a question-answer dataset designed specifically for evaluating LLMs in ecological and environmental sciences. The benchmark contains 1,130 QA pairs covering 16 environmental subjects, with items sourced from expert questionnaires and open-source authoritative materials. The dataset is annotated by content domain, difficulty, and question type (knowledge, calculation, reasoning), and the authors describe a cross-screening and expert validation process to improve quality and reliability.

The benchmark is intended for use as a standardized evaluation tool rather than as an intervention with human participants. It is positioned to support consistent, objective comparisons of AI models in environmental contexts and to promote more robust development of AI technologies for ecological and environmental applications. The paper concludes that the ELLE-QA Benchmark can help advance the standardization of AI assessment in this domain and provide a foundation for ongoing model evaluation.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a peer-reviewed benchmark/dataset paper with a clear methodology for constructing and validating QA items, but it does not evaluate an educational intervention or causal effect on learner outcomes. Evidence credibility is moderate for benchmark construction, not for impact on students.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper reports no K-12 learning or implementation outcomes; it introduces a dataset to assess model proficiency in environmental QA. There is no demonstrated impact on student achievement, engagement, or classroom practice.

interventions.use_case: Benchmarking generative AI / LLM systems and retrieval-augmented generation for answering ecological and environmental science questions, including domain-specific QA and reasoning tasks.
